mechanism_narrative: The federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is a leading indicator of accommodative monetary policy that consistently compresses discount rates and boosts equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 5.5% in a 3-month window, it signals a labor market slowdown that triggers equity market risk-off behavior, but subsequent economic policy responses lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite UNRATE > 5.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates a monetary policy signal: when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5% and UNRATE is above 5.5%, it indicates stimulative policy response to labor market weakness, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite FEDFUNDS < 0.5% and UNRATE > 5.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.5%), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced liquidity and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) are a leading indicator of economic expansion, which consistently drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 60% of instances, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 1000 thousand units in a 3-month window, it signals a housing market contraction that leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite HOUST < 1000, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: The interaction between housing starts (HOUST) and industrial production (INDPRO) creates a demand-supply signal: when HOUST is above 1050 and INDPRO is below 100, it indicates strong housing demand coupled with weak industrial output, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite HOUST > 1050 and INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During recessionary supply shocks (INDPRO < 100), the S&P 500 experiences negative returns over the next 60 trading days due to reduced economic activity and increased risk aversion.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO < 100, or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
